body: It survived two emulators to get there. Neither QEMU nor codex-vm modelled the update cycle: both answered every read with a clean value and swore no update was ever in progress. codex-vm does now.

author: reek
body: An unreadable clock returns -1. It is never an excuse to invent a time: the caller decides what to do without one, and that decision belongs to the caller.

author: reek
body: Wait out the update. The fuel is generous because the window is short and a stall here is a stall in a poll loop, not in a driver; exhausting it means the clock is not answering, which is a reading in itself and is reported as one.

author: reek
body: The seconds, or -1. Three gates: the update must be over, two reads must agree, and the answer must be a second.

author: reek
body: The unguarded read, kept ONLY so a test can demonstrate the hazard this chapter exists to close. Nothing in the boot path may call it.

author: val
body: MC146818: while the part updates its time registers once a second it raises Update-In-Progress (Status A bit 7) and the registers are UNDEFINED; real silicon returns junk, and a reader polling seconds without UIP sees many changes a second (the first-boot keyboard gate once counted thirty seconds in microseconds on a real board). So the reader (1) waits for UIP to clear, fuel-bounded, before touching a time register; (2) reads the register TWICE and requires the same answer; (3) rejects anything a second cannot be (0..59) as a bad read. Status B bit 2 set means binary, clear means BCD; most parts ship BCD, and assuming it mangles one that does not.
